items.stem: A real invoice is sent to the spam folder. What kind of mistake is that?

options.A: A perfect catch with no downside
options.B: A false alarm — flagged, but actually fine
options.C: Proof the filter can never err again

items.stem: Fraud slips into the "safe" pile. What kind of mistake is that?

options.A: A missed case — real problem, not flagged
options.B: A false alarm on a healthy payment

items.stem: Why do false alarms and missed cases often move in opposite directions?

options.A: Computers only allow one error type per year
options.B: Users must delete one type by law
options.C: Catching more real cases usually means flagging more fine ones too

items.stem: A clinic fears missing real disease more than scaring healthy people. What balance fits?

options.A: Accept almost no flags, even if many cases slip by
options.B: Accept more false alarms to catch more real cases
options.C: Turn the tool off and guess at random

items.stem: Which statement is most honest about systems that sort cases into labels?

options.A: They make pattern-based mistakes; none is perfect
options.B: A good one has a lifelong zero-error warranty
options.C: Errors only happen when the screen is dirty

items.stem: Why still use a sorter that sometimes errs?

options.A: Errors prove the tool is free
options.B: Humans never need a second look
options.C: It can still catch many cases faster, if people handle the costly edge cases

items.stem: In hiring screening, a strong candidate is auto-rejected. That is mainly:

options.A: A missed risk in airport security terms only
options.B: A false alarm on a person who was actually fine to advance

items.stem: What is a practical habit after any important automated flag?

options.A: Let a person review before big action
options.B: Assume the label is final forever
options.C: Hide the result from everyone involved

items.stem: Teaching a colleague the core idea, which line belongs?

options.A: "Pick either speed or coffee; errors are unrelated."
options.B: "If it is modern, both error types fall to zero."
options.C: "Two error types trade off, so we choose a balance and still review what matters."
